chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servants.
And He does not wrong anyone by the weight of an atom.
And He does not wrong anyone by the weight of an atom.

key_terms.ظَلَّامٍ: Tyrant or one who deals unjustly
key_terms.مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ: By the weight of an atom

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about Allah's justice and whether He wrongs His servants?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to establish the foundational Shia doctrine of divine justice (*al-Adl*), countering the Mu'tazila and Sunni schools on whether God's actions are inherently just. The Imam emphasizes that Allah’s justice is absolute and precise, extending even to the weight of an atom, thereby ensuring that no soul is burdened beyond its capacity or wronged in its recompense. This hadith serves as a critical theological proof for the belief that God’s decree is never arbitrary or tyrannical.
